articles.title: Red state Dem faces fury for suggesting illegal aliens should replace American workers
articles.summary: Hallie Shoffner said farmers would "trade five Americans just for one" illegal immigrant worker, drawing sharp criticism from Sen. Tom Cotton's campaign.
articles.body:
Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner faced backlash for suggesting that illegal alien workers are more valuable than American workers.

Shoffner's comments were made during an hour-long discussion on the "Free Arkansas Podcast" where she advocated for a pathway for illegal aliens to work legally in the U.S.

Shoffner's campaign manager defended her remarks, claiming they were taken out of context, while accusing Sen. Tom Cotton of misrepresenting the conversation.

A Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate from Arkansas is facing scrutiny for comments she recently made on a podcast suggesting that illegal alien workers are more valuable than their American counterparts.

"I want to talk about the fact that our immigration system is backlogged, bureaucratic and doesn't actually help anybody, including American employers who want folks who want to follow the law," Hallie Shoffner said on the "Free Arkansas Podcast" during an hour-long discussion about a wide spectrum of political issues.

Shoffner, a farmer, is running against Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark. in the deep red state.

She continued by saying she had a discussion with a fellow farmer, who she said was a Republican, about foreign labor.

"Labor is a huge issue, especially when you don't have a large workforce," she said. "And every farmer will tell you, 'yeah, at one point we did, or still do, employ undocumented immigrants.'" And it's absolutely ridiculous that these folks are being rounded up because they're hardworking people. They're some of the best people we know."

"And honestly, we'd trade five Americans just for one of them because of how hard they work," she said.

Shoffner then demanded a pathway for illegal aliens to work in the United States legally, claiming "when they're good workers, we pay them well, they're good workers, they spend money here [and] they have family here."

Cotton's campaign accused Shoffner of implying that she has hired illegal aliens.

"Hallie Shoffner's campaign isn't denying that she employed illegal aliens," campaign spokesman James Arnold told Fox News Digital. "They're also standing by Hallie Shoffner's claim that just one illegal immigrant is more valuable than five American citizens."

" Every Democrat running for Congress needs to answer if they agree with Hallie Shoffner's belief that illegal aliens are worth more than Americans," Arnold said.

In a response to Fox News Digital, Shoffner's campaign manager Anna-Lee Pittman said the candidate's comments were taken out of context, and accused Cotton of being unwilling to have a conversation to help "fix the immigration system."

Cotton, she said, "spends his days combing through video clips of Hallie Shoffner to find any possible inelegant phrase or line that he can chop up to misrepresent an hour-long conversation and present it with no context," noting that "[i]n this response, Shoffner relayed a conversation she had with another farmer about challenges with labor."

Shoffner once joined the chorus of left-wing calls to defund U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"I would vote to defund ICE as it exists right now," Shoffner said in an event June. "Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created not that long ago, and it no longer serves the purpose it was originally created for."

"I would not spend one more dime on ICE, because — not just because of the human dignity issue — but also the fact that it is now the largest law enforcement agency in the country," she said. "It has 10 times the budget of the organization that fights child sex trafficking."

But in a Facebook post earlier this month, the red state Democratic candidate changed her tune.

"I don't want to defund ICE, I want to reform it," she said.

Immigration is a hotbed issue heading into the midterm elections , as it was two years ago during President Donald Trump's campaign to occupy the White House for a second term.

The Trump administration has carried out immigration operations nationwide to arrest and deport illegal aliens, drawing blowback from Democrat politicians and activists.

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: superlive na TV Celular após ação de Lula no TSE | G1
articles.standfirst: Transmissão reuniu políticos de São Paulo no primeiro bloco, Mato Grosso do Sul e Paraná nos blocos seguintes; coligação de Lula pede ao TSE suspensão da plataforma por suposta falta de identificação eleitoral do conteúdo.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro reuniu aliados na TV Celular após a campanha de Lula pedir ao TSE a suspensão da plataforma por supostas irregularidades.
articles.body:
Guilherme Derrite (Progressistas), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), André do Prado (PL), Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) e Ricardo Nunes (MDB) participam de live promovida por Flávio Bolsonaro. — Foto: Reprodução/Youtube

O candidato do PL à Presidência da República, Flávio Bolsonaro , apresenta nesta quarta-feira (23) uma "superlive" com aliados e outros candidatos, principalmente ao Senado e a governos estaduais. O evento é transmitido de um estúdio na capital paulista, no canal TV Celular, no YouTube.

A TV Celular exibe programação ao vivo de forma contínua, reunindo participações de diversos políticos e apoiadores de Flávio.

A transmissão acontece dias depois de a campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) pedir ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) a suspensão da plataforma de vídeos do adversário . De acordo com a coligação de Lula , o conteúdo pode ser baixado e redistribuído nas redes sociais, operando como uma espécie de acervo digital de material de campanha, sem qualquer identificação de sua origem.

O argumento da coligação de Lula é que a plataforma não identifica que o conteúdo exibido é produzido pela campanha de Flávio, como exige a legislação eleitoral.

Na live, o candidato foi acompanhado no primeiro bloco por políticos e candidatos de São Paulo: integraram a mesa o governador Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ), o prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes ; os candidatos ao Senado André do Prado e Guilherme Derrite, além da candidata a deputada estadual Regina Nunes, esposa de Nunes.

Eles discutiram segurança pública, saúde, endividamento das famílias e criticaram o governo Lula, além de pedir voto para os candidatos a senador.

No segundo bloco, subiram ao palco nomes de Mato Grosso do Sul: Tereza Cristina, Eduardo Riedel e capitão Contar.

Capitão Contar (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Tereza Cristina (PP) e Eduardo Riedel (PP) participam de live promovida por Flávio Bolsonaro. — Foto: Reprodução/Youtube

articles.title: STF conclui julgamento e  decide igualar licença maternidade de mães biológica e adotivas  | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão unânime também proíbe distinção em razão de vínculo de trabalho. Decisão vale para licenças em andamento e novos pedidos.
articles.summary: Decisão unânime também proíbe distinção em razão de vínculo de trabalho. Decisão vale para licenças em andamento e novos pedidos.
articles.body:
O Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) decidiu nesta quarta-feira (23), por unanimidade, igualar os direitos de mães adotivas e biológicas em relação à licença maternidade.

🗓O julgamento começou na semana passada e foi concluído nesta quarta.

O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , relator da ação apresentada pela Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), foi acompanhado pelos ministros para fixar que todas as mães, sejam biológicas ou adotantes, terão direito a licença maternidade de idêntico conteúdo :

afastamento remunerado de 120 dias, prorrogável por mais 60 dias.

O prazo será contado a partir do 9º mês de gestação, do parto, da adoção, da obtenção da guarda para fins de adoção ou da alta hospitalar do recém-nascido ou da mãe, o que ocorrer por último.

➡️A regra valerá tanto para trabalhadoras contratadas pela Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), que rege as relações de trabalho na iniciativa privada, quanto para servidoras públicas submetidas a regime estatutário.

A decisão vale para novas licenças e para aquelas que já estão em andamento, não alcançando as que já terminaram.

Outra decisão dentro do julgamento foi a de proibir descriminação na concessão da licença com base no vínculo de trabalho da mãe.

“A meu ver, o regime jurídico, celetista, estatutário militar ou outro pode disciplinar inúmeros aspectos da relação de trabalho ou funcional, mas não pode alterar a intensidade da proteção constitucional devida à maternidade e à infância. A criança não necessita de mais ou menos cuidado conforme sua mãe seja empregada, servidora ou militar”, afirmou o ministro Kassio Nunes Marques .

Moraes negou apenas um pedido da PGR, que previa o compartilhamento de licença parental entre os integrantes do núcleo familiar.

Mulher grávida. — Foto: Imagem ilustrativa/Divulgação

Atualmente, mães biológicas que têm vínculo de trabalho estatutário na esfera federal têm 120 dias de licença remunerada.

Já as mães adotantes têm 90 dias de licença se a criança tiver até um ano e 30 dias se a criança tiver mais de 1 ano.

“Não há constitucionalidade nem em desfavor da maternidade adotiva nem tampouco uma segunda discriminação em relação à maternidade adotiva, o período de afastamento vai sendo graduado de acordo com a idade da criança adotada”, afirmou Moraes.

A CLT já equipara mães biológicas e adotantes para fins de licença maternidade, enquanto algumas leis estatutárias ainda mantêm diferenças formais para adotantes.

O STF vem entendendo que essa distinção viola a Constituição e a PGR pede a uniformização definitiva das regras para todas as categorias.

Em 2023, o Supremo decidiu que não é possível discriminar o tempo de licença-maternidade concedida à mãe biológica e à mãe adotante e citou princípios da dignidade humana, da igualdade entre filhos biológicos e adotados, da doutrina da proteção integral e dos princípios da prioridade e do melhor interesse da criança.

No entanto, a PGR sustenta que a decisão serviu de base apenas para órgãos do Poder Judiciário e não alcançou a administração pública. Por isso, a decisão não suspendeu a eficácia das leis em contrário e a discriminação continuou ocorrendo.

A ação pede a declaração de incompatibilidade das normas com a Constituição para, com isso, vincular tanto órgãos do Poder Judiciário, quanto a administração pública.

“Entende-se, portanto, ser cabível esta ação direta, que se dirige não somente a afastar a aplicação de disposições normativas que, na atualidade, acabam por configurar um tratamento discriminatório quanto à concessão de licença parental, como também fixar no plano jurídico-objetivo a tese de que o sistema de proteção parental, há de se submeter a um regime jurídico uniforme, independentemente do vínculo laboral da categoria que dele se beneficie”, argumenta a PGR.

Na semana passada, Moraes já havia votado e disse que “se todos são filhos, a mãe é mãe de todos, dos filhos naturais, biológicos, adotivos, então a licença maternidade deve ser igual para todos”.

Os ministros Cármen Lúcia , Flávio Dino e Dias Toffoli seguiram o entendimento.

Nesta quarta, os ministros Cristiano Zanin , André Mendonça , Kassio Nunes Marques, Luiz Fux , Gilmar Mendes e o presidente, Edson Fachin , seguiram o entendimento.

“Mãe é só uma e todo filho é único para nós. O filho é filho e pronto e essa desigualação poderia se constituir da pessoa se sentir distinta também, quando a pessoa contasse pra ela e tudo mais”, afirmou a ministra Cármen Lúcia.

articles.title: As ambições da China com IA em meio às conversas de Trump com Xi | G1
articles.standfirst: A BBC visitou a Mongólia Interior, no norte da China, onde a infraestrutura de IA do país avança rapidamente — em 'velocidade chinesa', segundo um trabalhador da região.
articles.summary: A BBC visitou a Mongólia Interior, no norte da China, onde a infraestrutura de IA do país avança rapidamente — em 'velocidade chinesa', segundo um trabalhador da região.
articles.body:
Ambições da China com IA — Foto: Wong Yu Liang/ Getty via BBC

Nas imensas pastagens da Mongólia Interior, no norte da China, agricultores estão colhendo belas batatas ao lado de novos vizinhos: enormes blocos retangulares que alimentam as plataformas chinesas de inteligência artificial (IA) .

A região de Ulanqab, com suas estepes e vulcões, é uma fronteira digital improvável.

Ela foi oficialmente, por anos, a "capital da batata" da China. Mas, agora, seus campos também se tornaram o local de construção de diversos centros de dados, no momento em que os presidentes dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , e da China, Xi Jinping , se reúnem para discutir, entre outras coisas, a segurança da IA.

Centenas de trabalhadores, com seus capacetes amarelos, carregam equipamentos pesados para o local da construção, enquanto o soldador lança faíscas dos andaimes de metal. Acima deles, enormes guindastes se movimentam com precisão para construir os telhados e homens se equilibram em escadas para rebocar a alvenaria.

"Esta é a velocidade chinesa", brinca um trabalhador. Ele descreve seu país como "maníaco pela infraestrutura", rindo enquanto se afasta.

"Existe uma fase todos os anos. Esta é a segunda fase", explica um engenheiro elétrico. "Haverá muitas outras em seguida."

A inteligência artificial está no centro da competição entre a China e os Estados Unidos . Para isso, o poder de computação dos data centers da região é fundamental.

Para o Partido Comunista Chinês, estes edifícios são fundamentais para a segurança nacional e econômica do país. Quando estiverem terminados, eles ajudarão a guiar sua missão de incluir a IA em 90% das indústrias e da sociedade até 2030 .

A inteligência artificial está no centro da competição entre a China e os Estados Unidos. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A China não está apenas construindo a infraestrutura. O país também está criando um conjunto de talentos.

Jovens engenheiros e pesquisadores, agora, observam o país como um local repleto de oportunidades, em parte, devido às tensões com os Estados Unidos e às restrições à imigração impostas por Donald Trump , que azedaram o "sonho americano" de muitos chineses.

"Menos estudantes e pesquisadores estão se mudando para os Estados Unidos e mais estão retornando para a China. É algo muito claro", explica Jack Zhang, da Universidade de Ciência e Tecnologia da China.

Ele próprio foi recrutado por um programa de alto nível, depois de estudar na Universidade Yale, nos EUA, e em Cambridge, no Reino Unido.

"Eu quis levar parte do trabalho de IA que fazia no laboratório e aplicá-lo à saúde e medicina humana", ele conta.

"Isso exige mais recursos, mais pessoas e, às vezes, mais apoio do governo. E pode ser difícil ter acesso a isso no exterior."

A expansão das capacidades chinesas em relação à IA é uma das razões que levaram Washington a afirmar que não quer interromper seus desenvolvimentos no setor, mesmo com os alertas da indústria sobre os eventuais perigos da alta velocidade do avanço da tecnologia.

"Quem vencer a IA, vence", declarou Trump na semana passada.

O CEO (diretor-executivo) da empresa de IA Anthropic, Dario Amodei, pediu que seja mantida a proibição , liderada pelos Estados Unidos , da venda de chips e equipamentos avançados para a China. Para ele, uma liderança chinesa "causaria graves riscos para os Estados Unidos e o mundo".

Esta afirmação não é o que o presidente Xi gostará de ouvir ao chegar a Washington, nesta quarta-feira (23/9). O jornal estatal chinês Global Times, que ecoa as opiniões de Pequim, rejeitou os temores dos Estados Unidos como sendo parte de um "roteiro da Guerra Fria" para "conter" a ascensão da China.

Mas a preocupação chinesa não é apenas alcançar os Estados Unidos . Pequim também está promovendo um modelo alternativo.

O próprio Xi vem incentivando as empresas chinesas de IA a desenvolver modelos mais baratos de código aberto, que permitam às pessoas, empresas e países modificá-los conforme desejarem.

Esta estratégia também opõe os modelos chineses aos desenvolvedores americanos, como a OpenAI e a Anthropic, que usam técnicas de modelos fechados, mantendo seus elementos de design em segredo.

Um dos motivos que levaram Pequim a adotar este sistema é que funcionou bem para eles. E, compartilhando a tecnologia, as empresas chinesas de IA conseguiram inovar rapidamente.

Tudo isso ajudou a China a superar um dos seus maiores desafios: a falta de acesso a chips avançados, que ajudariam o país com seu maior poder de computação.

Mas Pequim também quer maior participação para definir as regras que regem a IA. Xi vem pedindo repetidamente maior regulamentação e um enquadramento global a ser seguido pelos demais.

Com o aumento dos apelos pela segurança da IA, a cúpula desta semana na Casa Branca é especialmente significativa.

Será que os dois lados conseguirão colaborar para a regulamentação da IA? Seria realista uma eventual negociação para reduzir a velocidade do seu desenvolvimento?

Certamente não parece ser o caso quando se observa lugares como Ulanqab, onde as ambições chinesas em relação à IA estão tomando forma.

A China está construindo centenas de data centers para empresas como Huawei , ByteDance e DeepSeek , em províncias escassamente povoadas: Ulanqab, Ningxia e Gansu, no norte, e Guizhou, no sudoeste do país.

O país já instalou enormes capacidades de produção de energia renovável (eólica e solar) naquelas regiões, onde a terra é mais barata e o clima é mais frio e, por isso, a demanda por água é menor.

Os novos vizinhos dos produtores de batatas da Mongólia Interior são fundamentais para a corrida chinesa pela IA contra os Estados Unidos. — Foto: BBC

Tudo isso não significa que não haja preocupações, nem desvantagens.

A China quer que a maior parte dos seus centros de dados sejam alimentados por energia verde até 2030, mas parte da sua rede elétrica ainda é alimentada por carvão.

O abastecimento de água ainda é uma preocupação nas áridas regiões da Mongólia Interior.

Aldeias inteiras foram relocadas, mas é difícil calcular o número e a compensação oferecida aos moradores. É um tema que poucas pessoas discutem, pois pode ser perigoso expressar abertamente seus receios.

"Estes big data não têm absolutamente nada a ver com as pessoas comuns", diz um morador local, falando de forma anônima, longe das câmeras. "Que benefícios eles nos trouxeram?"

Ele afirma que poucos moradores locais encontraram empregos ali. Outros nos contaram sobre seu receio de que sua terra seja tomada e que eles não possam mais ganhar a vida com a agricultura.

Mas também há os otimistas, como um homem que se identificou à reportagem com o sobrenome Zhang. Ele estava ao lado dos colhedores de batatas, em um campo perto dos data centers.

Zhang conta que seus filhos conseguiram encontrar empregos ali.

"A China, agora, está na vanguarda do mundo", afirma ele.

"Não é como nos anos 1960, quando estávamos relativamente atrasados. A China está fazendo tudo certo, agora. Seja no desenvolvimento econômico ou em outras áreas, ela está se saindo bem."

Zhang é otimista sobre a política chinesa em relação à IA e conta que seus filhos conseguiram encontrar empregos nos novos centros de dados. — Foto: BBC

As pesquisas parecem indicar que existe pouca oposição à IA ou à sua adoção disseminada, em comparação com muitos outros países. Mas é difícil avaliar estes números, em um panorama de forte censura.

Pequim tem deixado muito claro que observa a IA como solução para sua força de trabalho envelhecida e está automatizando rapidamente sua produção e suas indústrias. Isso vem gerando ansiedade em relação à perda de empregos, o que também é algo difícil de avaliar.

Mas este é um país que forma cerca de cinco milhões de profissionais no setor de ciência e tecnologia todos os anos, o que é muito mais que os cerca de 500 mil formandos anuais dos Estados Unidos .

E, com um número maior deles permanecendo na China, surge um ecossistema de inovação crescente.

O desenvolvedor de IA Dang Ronghao, de 27 anos, trabalha para uma das empresas líderes em tecnologia. Ele afirma que as universidades chinesas estão ficando mais abertas, o que permite a ele conversar com pesquisadores de todo o mundo, da sua base em Xangai, no leste da China.

"Observei pesquisas combinando IA com fusão nuclear, IA com astrofísica, IA com novos materiais e IA com o desenvolvimento de novos medicamentos", ele conta. "Acho que estamos entrando em uma boa era."

Ainda assim, alguns defendem que a China ainda recompensa a conformidade, não o questionamento.

"Não é tão aberto quanto eu gostaria", afirma o professor Liu Jun, do Departamento de Ciência de Dados e Estatística da Universidade Tsinghua, em Pequim. Ele estudou nas Universidades de Stanford e Harvard, nos Estados Unidos .

"Continuo incentivando os estudantes aqui a fazer mais perguntas, a questionar mais, mas é difícil mudar. Acho que, em parte, é a cultura e, em parte, é o sistema."

A China considera a IA uma solução para sua força de trabalho envelhecida. — Foto: BBC

Longe dos laboratórios onde o professor Liu e outros questionam as fronteiras da IA, muitos cidadãos chineses ainda enfrentam problemas econômicos mais imediatos, como a lentidão da economia, o desemprego cada vez maior dos jovens, a queda dos gastos da população e a disparada dos preços dos imóveis.

E, nas regiões rurais, o envelhecimento da população é outro problema crescente.

" Big data e tudo o mais... muito bom. Mas não tem nada a ver comigo", afirma um agricultor da Mongólia Interior, enquanto avança em uma carroça para observar suas ovelhas.

Ele afirma que não usa a IA para nada. E raramente usa a internet.

A tela do seu telefone celular está quebrada e o wifi vem de um dongle de bolso. Ele paga pouco mais de 40 yuans (US$ 6, cerca de R$ 31) por mês.

Agricultores locais empregam pouco a IA porque raramente usam a internet. — Foto: BBC

"Não mudou nada para mim, na verdade", ele conta. "Não sei sobre o futuro."

Este tipo de ceticismo pode vir a ser um desafio para Pequim.

Existem tantas mudanças ocorrendo por aqui e em todo o país, mas é difícil saber quantas pessoas são tão dedicadas quanto seus líderes, neste futuro repleto de tecnologia.

articles.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo Senado no CE | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) foi encomendada pela TV Verdes Mares. Na pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos pré-candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores, 65% estão indecisos.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) foi encomendada pela TV Verdes Mares.
articles.body:
Quaest no CE para o Senado. — Foto: Sistema Verdes Mares (SVM) e Agência Câmara

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado no Ceará . O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Verdes Mares.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest — em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados —, 65% estão indecisos, porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos. Veja os números abaixo:

Cid Gomes (PSB): 25% (eram 23% em 4 de setembro)

Agora, veja os resultados que consideram apenas as respostas para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda.

Em branco/nulo/não vai votar: 12% (eram 12%)

Para 68% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 31% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

A Quaest ouviu 900 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 19 e 22 de setembro. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é CE-08268/2026.

articles.title: Morador de Salmourão morre por leishmaniose; é 2º óbito em SP em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Morte ocorreu em julho, mas foi contabilizada nas estatísticas estaduais somente agora. Prefeitura realizou ações de orientação no bairro onde ele morava.
articles.summary: A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Salmourão (SP) confirmou a morte de um homem de 58 anos por leishmaniose. O óbito passou a constar nas estatísticas do Governo do Estado.
articles.body:
A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Salmourão (SP) confirmou a morte de um homem de 58 anos por leishmaniose. O óbito passou a constar nas estatísticas do Governo do Estado de São Paulo e é o segundo registrado pela doença no Estado em 2026.

Segundo a prefeitura, a morte ocorreu em julho, mas foi contabilizada nos dados estaduais somente agora.

De acordo com a Secretaria de Saúde, o homem ficou internado no Hospital das Clínicas (HC) de Marília (SP) e já estava com diagnóstico de leishmaniose quando morreu. Ele também tinha complicações de saúde e era cardíaco .

Segundo informações divulgadas pelo município, este é o único caso de leishmaniose em humanos registrado em Salmourão no período apontado pelo boletim estadual, e corresponde ao paciente que morreu.

Após o registro do caso, a equipe de vetores do município, acompanhada por uma veterinária da prefeitura, realizou ações de manejo e orientação no bairro onde o homem morava, com distribuição de panfletos aos moradores.

Além do óbito registrado em Salmourão, o Governo do Estado contabiliza outra morte por leishmaniose, em Fernandópolis (SP), na região de São José do Rio Preto (SP). Os dois casos passaram a integrar os registros estaduais da doença em 2026.

Transmissão da leishmaniose é feita pelo Mosquito-palha — Foto: Divulgação

Entre as orientações repassadas à população está a necessidade de evitar o acúmulo de material orgânico, como galhos e folhas, além de manter os quintais limpos.

A recomendação também inclui evitar o acúmulo de lixo e água, e utilizar repelente como forma de prevenção.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde reforçou que as medidas são importantes para a proteção da população.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro busca liderança no 1º turno para atrair Centrão | G1
articles.standfirst: Aliados de Lula avaliam que reajuste do Bolsa Família e MP de combate às bets devem garantir primeiro lugar no dia 4 de outubro, o que deve segurar o apoio do Centrão ao petista.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro planeja liderar o primeiro turno para atrair o Centrão, enquanto Lula aposta no Bolsa Família e combate às bets para manter vantagem.
articles.body:
Dentro da campanha do candidato do PL , Flávio Bolsonaro , a estratégia é terminar o primeiro turno à frente do presidente Lula , criando um sentimento de favoritismo capaz de atrair a maior parte dos eleitores dos demais candidatos de direita, como Ronaldo Caiado ( PSD ), Romeu Zema ( Novo ), Augusto Cury ( Avante ) e Renan Santos ( Missão ).

A equipe de Flávio espera, inclusive, algo que faltou no primeiro turno, o apoio oficial dos partidos do Centrão.

Os mais otimistas na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro falam até na possibilidade de vencer a eleição já no primeiro turno, com a criação de uma onda a favor do que chamam de "voto útil" nesta reta final.

Jogam contra essa estratégia as últimas iniciativas do presidente Lula, que já anunciou um reajuste no benefício do Bolsa Família e vai assinar medida provisória de combate às bets no Brasil , o que tem amplo apoio entre os brasileiros.

Segundo pesquisa Datafolha, o candidato do PL tem o potencial de atrair, num segundo turno, 43% das intenções de voto de eleitores de Romeu Zema, Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado e Augusto Cury.

Já Lula atrairia 30% destes eleitores dos candidatos da direita. Flávio Bolsonaro se dá melhor entre eleitores de Zema e Renan Santos, com empate técnico no eleitorado de Ronaldo Caiado e Augusto Cury.

Na campanha do presidente Lula, todo esforço será feito para que Lula termine o primeiro turno à frente de Flávio Bolsonaro.

Segundo aliados de Lula, a MP sobre bets vai atingir principalmente o eleitorado feminino, garantindo um apoio ainda maior neste segmento do eleitorado, considerado crucial para a definição da eleição deste ano. O petista tem vantagem entre as mulheres, que são as mais críticas aos jogos de apostas online.

"As pesquisas mostram hoje um forte sentimento contrário às bets. Lula vai trabalhar com esse sentimento a seu favor. Isso vai pesar e muito nesta reta final", diz um interlocutor do presidente da República, confiante que o petista terminará o primeiro turno à frente de Flávio Bolsonaro.

Segundo esse auxiliar, sair na liderança no segundo turno vai segurar o Centrão e também influenciar até na atuação de aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno.

A avaliação é que, em São Paulo, por exemplo, o governador Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ) ganhe no primeiro turno e não faça grande esforço em favor do candidato do PL na fase final. Afinal, Tarcísio deve ser candidato à Presidência da República em 2030 e não gostaria de ter Flávio Bolsonaro no Palácio do Planalto no próximo ano.

articles.title: Corregedoria do CNJ cancela R$ 4,7 bilhões em precatórios de empresas que venderam crédito ao Banco Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Usinas citadas na decisão aparecem em lista encontrada no celular de Vorcaro como ‘precatórios a receber’. Uma delas estavam em contrato de escritório da ‘Turma do Kassio’.
articles.summary: Usinas citadas na decisão aparecem em lista encontrada no celular de Vorcaro como ‘precatórios a receber’. Uma delas estavam em contrato de escritório da ‘Turma do Kassio’.
articles.body:
O corregedor nacional de Justiça, Benedito Gonçalves, determinou, em decisão divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23), o cancelamento do pagamento de R$ 4,7 bilhões em precatórios do setor sucroalcooleiro — ligados a indústrias de açúcar e etanol — e a devolução do montante à Conta Única do Tesouro Nacional .

🔎 Precatórios são dívidas que governos (União, estados e municípios) são obrigados a pagar após perderem uma ação na Justiça de forma definitiva, sem possibilidade de recurso.

A decisão atende a pedido de liminar (ou seja, provisório) da Advocacia Geral da União (AGU) e se refere a 16 precatórios de três usinas que aparecem em uma lista encontrada no celular do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do extinto Banco Master, como “precatórios a receber” .

O dinheiro estava depositado em contas judiciais desde 2023 ( leia mais abaixo ).

A decisão do corregedor suspendeu decisões da Presidência do Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região (TRF-1). Dessa forma, o tribunal terá cinco dias para cancelar os precatórios e restituir os valores , com seus rendimentos, ao Tesouro.

Companhia Açucareira Vale do Ceará Mirim.

A Usina Capricho consta também em um contrato de prestação de serviços advocatícios entre o Banco Master e um escritório de advocacia para atuar em processos relacionados a precatórios.

O documento, também encontrado no celular de Vorcaro, é de março de 2024. A minuta de prestação de serviços com o escritório "Queiroga, Vieira, Queiroz & Ramos", de Camilla Ramos, esposa do desembargador Newton Ramos, do Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região (TRF-1).

Camila e Newton eram chamados por Vorcaro de “Turma do KN”, iniciais que seriam do ministro da Suprema Corte, Kassio Nunes Marques. Em nota, o ministro afirmou que "nunca autorizou ninguém a falar em nome dele".

Corregedoria do CNJ cancela R$ 4,7 bilhões em precatórios de empresas que venderam crédito ao Banco Master — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O corregedor entendeu haver risco de dano aos cofres públicos. O dinheiro estava depositado em contas judiciais desde dezembro de 2023, referente a precatórios expedidos antes do fim da fase processual de execução.

Segundo o CNJ, essa modalidade de “precatório bloqueado” não possui amparo legal e contraria decisão anterior do próprio Conselho.

“Mais de um ano depois da ordem de cancelamento, esses requisitórios continuam registrados como precatórios bloqueados, com R$ 4,7 bilhões mantidos em contas judiciais. Quando o Juízo de origem aplicou a orientação do Supremo Tribunal Federal, convergente com a deste Conselho, a medida foi parcialmente sustada sob o argumento de que o bloqueio bastaria para proteger o erário”, afirmou Gonçalves.

“Esse é justamente o entendimento que o Plenário afastou ao reconhecer que o precatório bloqueado não tem amparo legal”, acrescentou.

articles.title: Marina Silva apoia expansão de biocombustíveis e melhora na saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata ao Senado pela Rede é a terceira a participar da série de entrevistas da TV TEM com os mais bem colocados na pesquisa Quaest de intenções de voto.
articles.summary: A candidata ao Senado por São Paulo, Marina Silva (Rede), disse apoiar uma expansão do mercado para os biocombustíveis produzidos no estado e defendeu o fortalecimento da saúde.
articles.body:
A candidata ao Senado por São Paulo, Marina Silva (Rede), disse apoiar uma expansão do mercado para os biocombustíveis produzidos no estado e defendeu o fortalecimento da rede de atenção básica de saúde para melhorar os atendimentos.

Marina Silva foi a terceira a participar da série de entrevistas da TV TEM com os candidatos ao Senado mais bem colocados na pesquisa Quaest de intenções de voto. Guilherme Derrite (Progressistas) e Simone Tebet (PSB) já foram entrevistados. André do Prado (PL) ainda participa. As entrevistas são conduzidas pela jornalista Danielle Borba e vão ao ar no Tem Notícias - 1ª Edição , entre os dias 21 e 24 de setembro.

A candidata tem 68 anos, nasceu em Rio Branco (AC) e construiu uma trajetória política ligada principalmente às pautas ambientais e sociais. Já foi vereadora, deputada estadual e senadora por dois mandatos. Atuou como ministra do Meio Ambiente e disputou a presidência da República três vezes. Também foi eleita deputada federal e voltou ao Ministério do Meio Ambiente antes de concorrer a uma das vagas de São Paulo ao Senado.

À TV TEM , Marina Silva afirmou que, com a experiência acumulada como ministra, pode ajudar a expandir o mercado para os biocombustíveis de São Paulo.

“Nós temos a oportunidade de fazer com que os biocombustíveis brasileiros se transformem em um combustível de transição e eu posso ajudar a abrir mercados. São Paulo também tem base tecnológica para fazer mais pesquisas sobre hidrogênio verde e aumentar nossa geração eólica e solar”, argumentou.

A candidata também falou sobre segurança pública, área em que vê a necessidade de mais integração entre as polícias e outros órgãos de comando e controle, como a Receita Federal. Marina Silva declarou que os agentes de segurança deveriam ser melhor remunerados. “Não faz sentido um estado como São Paulo ter um policial que ganha menos do que em outras unidades da federação com menos recursos”.

Marina Silva foi a terceira a participar de série de entrevistas da TV TEM com os candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

Na entrevista, a candidata sustentou a necessidade de fortalecer os atendimentos básicos de saúde no estado e, ao mesmo tempo, viabilizar mais recursos para os hospitais regionais que atendem média e alta complexidade.

“Se você não tiver um sistema que funciona, com atendimento básico de saúde, média e alta complexidade, vai colapsar em algum desses lugares. Você tem que pensar o sistema sem negligenciar nenhuma dessas partes. Quando isso funciona, você tem um desafogamento daqueles que deveriam estar cuidando de ações mais complexas dentro do sistema de saúde”, apontou.

Segundo Marina Silva, o processo de concessões para Organizações Sociais de Saúde (OSS) trouxe problemas para a área no estado e deveria ser revisto.

A candidata frisou, por fim, ter propostas para o combate à violência contra a mulher e o enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas. “São 177 municípios paulistas que são afetados pelos eventos climáticos extremos”, concluiu.

articles.title: Michelle Bolsonaro tem alta após crise de enxaqueca em Brasília | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata ao Senado pelo DF havia sido internada na terça-feira (22) após apresentar quadro de enxaqueca refratária. Ela faz tratamento há dois meses.
articles.summary: Michelle Bolsonaro recebeu alta nesta quarta-feira (23) após ser internada em Brasília com enxaqueca refratária, condição que a candidata trata há dois meses.
articles.body:
Michelle Bolsonaro — Foto: Eduardo F.S. Lima/Ato Press/Estadão Conteúdo

A candidata ao Senado pelo Distrito Federal Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) teve alta hospitalar nesta quarta-feira (23).

Ela havia sido internada na terça-feira (22), em Brasília , após apresentar um quadro de enxaqueca refratária, que não melhorou com o tratamento, segundo o Hospital DF Star.

Nas redes sociais, a candidata fez uma publicação anunciando sua melhora. "De alta, graças ao meu bom Deus! Obrigada pelas orações, carinho e por todas as mensagens que recebi", escreveu.

Na ocasião, ela passou por um bloqueio anestésico dos nervos cranianos e pericranianos devido à persistência das dores.

A internação aconteceu na véspera da convenção do Partido Liberal (PL) no Distrito Federal, que oficializou as candidaturas de Michelle Bolsonaro e da deputada federal Bia Kicis ao Senado.

articles.title: Republicans say Democrats are extremists. These Democrats want to convince voters that's not true
articles.summary: As Democrats try to take back control of Congress, they're trying a familiar tactic to win over voters in conservative areas — they're criticizing their own...
articles.body:
COLUMBIA, S.C. (AP) — As Democrats try to take back control of Congress , they're trying a familiar tactic to win over voters in conservative areas — they're criticizing their own party.

They're complaining about former President Joe Biden, promising to work with President Donald Trump to secure the border, insisting they'll never defund the police and criticizing democratic socialists as too extreme.

Taking shots at the left is one way that Democrats are trying to distance themselves from their party's tarnished brand. It's also a reflection of how the midterms are increasingly playing out in red states. Although progressives notched notable wins in Democratic primaries this year, the path to a majority in the House and the Senate runs through places where Trump won two years ago, such as North Carolina, Alaska, Kansas and Iowa.

"You need to own values that are where the center of the party is," said Adam Frisch, the finance director for Welcome PAC, which tries to boost Democrats in Republican-leaning districts. He previously ran twice for Congress in Colorado.

North Carolina's Cooper boasts of bipartisanship

Known for forging compromise with the Republican-led legislature during his two terms as governor, Roy Cooper argues in his Senate campaign that Democrats should be willing to do the same in Congress.

Cooper also served as state attorney general, and one of his ads says he "toughened bail laws, went after drug dealers pushing fentanyl and said, 'No way do we defund the police.'" Another says Cooper "bucked his own party to oppose defunding the police" and "partnered" with the Republican president to crack down on drugs.

Conservatives and allies of Republican nominee Michael Whatley , former chairman of the Republican National Committee, have tried to link Cooper to national progressive figures like New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, an independent who caucuses with Democrats.

When Cooper entered the race more than a year ago, the Senate Leadership Fund — a Republican super PAC affiliated with Senate Majority Leader John Thune — swiftly attacked him by saying he "masquerades as a moderate" but is "just another radical, D.C. liberal in disguise."

Earlier this month, Cooper explained a bit of his strategy to CNN, saying that he felt that "there are enough people who are skeptical of national Democrats" in North Carolina, a factor he cited in the state's tendency to elect Democrats to statewide offices more often than its congressional offices.

Alaska's Peltola and Iowa's Turek want distance from national Democrats

In Alaska , former Rep. Mary Peltola has tried to steer the same centrist path as in her House campaigns, reviving her "fish, family, freedom" slogan and expressing support for Second Amendment rights and border security — two issues that traditionally resonate with more conservative voters.

"I'll take on anyone, including Democrats, anyone in the Lower 48 who doesn't understand what Alaska needs," she said in one campaign advertisement that mentioned her support for the massive Willow oil project on Alaska's petroleum-rich North Slope that was opposed by environmentalists. "When both parties are attacking you, you're doing something right."

Peltola's tone hasn't kept incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan from seeking to align Peltola with "D.C. Democrats," as well as characterizing her as ineffective during her time in Congress.

Meanwhile, in Iowa , Democratic nominee Josh Turek has emphasized his commitment to bipartisanship, highlighting hundreds of times he voted with Republicans as a state legislator. He represented a district won by Trump, and he leaned on that experience in this year's Senate race as evidence that he could appeal to independent and moderate Republican voters in November.

As he vies with Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson for the seat of retiring Republican Sen. Joni Ernst , Turek is also running an ad decrying the U.S.' "broken immigration system," saying, "I'll work with anyone to fix it, including President Trump."

After Turek won the nomination, Hinson told delegates at Republicans' state convention that he was "masquerading as a moderate," calling her opponent "a far-left fraud."

Hamilton says Kansas is very distant from Washington's 'extreme politics'

Pastor of a Kansas megachurch, Democratic Senate nominee Adam Hamilton describes himself as a centrist, running partly on "bringing people together" and noting that his congregation is nearly evenly split among Democrats, Republicans and independents.

That's the tenor Hamilton has brought to his campaign against Republican incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, running ads noting that Kansas is "proud of being in the middle politically" and "about a million miles away from the extreme politics of Washington that are tearing us apart and driving up prices."

"On one side, the far left pushes socialism and open borders," he said. "On the other side, Roger Marshall gives us higher gas and grocery prices, while slashing our healthcare."

In a debate earlier this month at the Kansas state fair, Hamilton also wasn't shy to blame Biden for immigration problems while also criticizing Trump's policies.

"Immigration at the border under Biden was a disaster," Hamilton said. "That is how we ended up where we are today."

Marshall has said Hamilton is "too woke for Kansas."

Sand decries parties as 'two private clubs' in Iowa governor's race

It's not just Senate contests in which Democratic candidates are seeking to chart a new course.

Back in Iowa — where Democrats see an opportunity to win in a once-competitive state, with high costs, manufacturing job losses and a struggling agricultural economy weighing on voters — Democrat Rob Sand says he can win over independents and Republicans frustrated with party politics.

Central to his campaign message is the premise that America's political system is broken "largely because it's run by two private clubs" — the two major parties — "the well fed versus the fed up."

Republican nominee Zach Lahn has said Sand's critique of his own party isn't genuine. Appearing on the "Ruthless" podcast this summer, he said that Democrats "are realizing that their ideas don't sell" and "have to pretend to be somebody they're not."

articles.title: Ken Paxton’s estranged wife tells GOP women: Vote Republican ‘even if we’re mad’
articles.summary: Texas state Rep. Angela Paxton (R) told a group of conservative women to vote Republican “even if we’re mad at them,” marking the first time she has publicly...
articles.body:
Texas state Rep. Angela Paxton (R) told a group of conservative women to vote Republican "even if we're mad at them," marking the first time she has publicly weighed in on her estranged husband's Senate race as he trails in the polls.

Paxton filed for divorce in July 2025 from Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) "on biblical grounds," accusing him of adultery. She has largely stayed silent on his Senate race, which has divided Texas Republicans.

Appearing at a Texas Federation of Republican Women meeting, Angela Paxton warned the group that when voting, they should consider that "the party comes with the person."

"Because we have more control over that seat and the future when we control the seat, when it's still in the family, even if we're mad at it," she said. "But if we lose it to the other team, the nuances that we want to fix with maybe a certain candidate are nothing compared to what it's going to take to get it back, right?"

She added that when Republicans diverge from the party, there are repercussions.

"They're [Democratic candidates] not like a stand-alone thing, like a menu item. We have more control when it's our party," Paxton continued. "We have more ability than influence, and that person is attached to our party."

During the primaries in May, Paxton urged Texas voters to turn out on the state's primary election day in a social media post , but she notably did not mention her former husband's race.

The Texas Senate race is shaping up to be among the most expensive in the country, with Democratic candidate James Talarico narrowly leading Paxton in recent polls. GOP groups are starting to pour money into the race, which is key to Republican hopes of maintaining Senate control.

Ken Paxton, who defeated Sen. John Cornyn (Texas) in the GOP Senate primary, brings notable baggage to the race. The Texas attorney general has been dogged by scandal, previously facing impeachment in the Texas state House on corruption charges before being acquitted in the state Senate.

His controversies have led former aides and attorneys who worked for him to support Talarico — including Dan Cogdell, who helped lead Ken Paxton's defense during his impeachment trial.

A recent poll showed Talarico was leading Paxton in the Senate race, with 46 percent of respondents supporting the Democrat and 43 percent backing the Republican.

Paxton's campaign and Angela Paxton's office did not respond immediately to The Hill's request for comment.

articles.title: Trump rails against CNN’s Collins and media ‘sleazebags’ over UN presence
articles.summary: President Trump ripped CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins on Tuesday for covering him despite banning the network along with MS NOW and Politico from the White House. “You should not be here covering me,” Trump told the chief White House correspondent before his speech at the United Nations General Assembly after she asked when the war…
articles.body:
President Trump ripped CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins on Tuesday for covering him despite banning the network along with MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

“You should not be here covering me,” Trump told the chief White House correspondent before his speech at the United Nations General Assembly after she asked when the war with Iran would end.

“You said you weren’t going to cover me,” he continued. “You shouldn’t be covering me.”

Collins later explained she was credentialed by the U.N. Following her exchange with the president, the host noted that CNN “never said we were not going to cover the president.”

“We will continue to cover the president and his speech and as he meets with world leaders today, just not with a TV camera from one of the five major networks in the room,” she added.

CNN is part of the five-network White House TV pool along with ABC News, CBS News, Fox News and NBC News. After CNN was barred from the White House grounds and unable to carry out its scheduled pool duties Monday, the other major networks suspended pool coverage in solidarity.

Trump later tore into Collins in a lengthy Truth Social post , calling her a “Third Rate ‘Reporter’” while questioning why she and other journalists from the targeted outlets were covering his New York appearance.

“All of the SLEAZEBAGS, like Third Rate ‘Reporter,’ Kaitlan Collins, of Fake News CNN, a truly unhappy person, said they weren’t going to be covering me,” he wrote late Tuesday.

“Why was she there? She’s got a ‘TRUMP’ addiction, and so does CNN and MSDNC,” he continued, referring to MS NOW, formerly known as MSNBC. “They’re all sick, treasonous, and demented!”

The news organizations sued the Trump administration to restore their access, citing First Amendment violations. The case will go before U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first administration, on Wednesday afternoon.

The president signaled he expects to lose the case and deflected on whether the White House would follow the eventual ruling. The Justice Department in a late Tuesday filing argued that White House access was a “privilege” and pressed the judge to dismiss the challenge.

Kelly was the judge that oversaw a previous legal challenge brought by CNN reporter Jim Acosta after the White House revoked his access to the complex.

Trump noted this again in his Truth Social post, saying the outlets have a key advantage in the case with Kelly assigned to it.

“The ‘good news’ is that they have a great, for them, and totally disloyal Judge,” he wrote, referring to Kelly.

CNN, along with MS NOW and Politico, have still been able to cover Trump at the U.N. using credentials issued independently by the international body.

articles.title: Newsom's admission that infamous COVID move was 'insane' triggers viral fury: 'We all told you'
articles.summary: Gavin Newsom called California's COVID beach closures "insane" in hindsight, sparking fierce backlash from critics who say they warned him then.
articles.body: Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom generated fierce online backlash after admitting the state's decision to close beaches amid the COVID-19 pandemic was "insane in hindsight" during an interview with CNN's Jake Tapper released this month. "Look, everyone's a genius in hindsight, so, you know, coulda, woulda," Newsom told Tapper while fly-fishing in a Montana river. When asked what he would have done differently, Newsom said people initially treated the pandemic like a "Purell-based crisis," spending too much time on hand sanitizer shortages and price gouging instead of the virus. He added the beach closures are one of several decisions he regrets. ‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE "The idea that we closed beaches was insane in hindsight," he said, before adding that he also regrets that the state's largest public school systems remained closed longer than they should have. The clip ignited a social media firestorm, with conservatives and some Californians accusing Newsom of acknowledging mistakes they argued were obvious during the pandemic. In a post on X, Republican former Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt wrote, "No, Gavin. It was insane then. We all told you it was insane then. You knew it was insane then. You're just an insane person." "Remember when I sued you in both state and federal court to open the beaches of Orange County that you maliciously closed, and you lifted the order so as to moot our cases before the hearings?" Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon posted on X. "You knew it back then too, Governor." FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES "Gavin Newsom had a man arrested for paddleboarding alone because apparently that put him at risk of getting COVID," Benny Johnson, host of "The Benny Show," posted on X. articles.title: ICE leaves US citizen injured on ground in mistaken identity incident
articles.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) left a U.S. citizen from Evanston, Ill., injured on the ground after he was detained in an incident of mistaken identity on Sunday, according to local police. A Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson told The Hill on Wednesday that during an operation in Evanston, ICE officers found a man…
articles.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) left a U.S. citizen from Evanston, Ill., injured on the ground after he was detained in an incident of mistaken identity on Sunday, according to local police.

A Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson told The Hill on Wednesday that during an operation in Evanston, ICE officers found a man “who resembled the target.” They identified themselves, but the man did not identify himself.

“ICE officers relied on their training and later left the scene without further incident once the individual finally identified himself,” the spokesperson said. “When ICE officers offered the individual assistance, he refused.”

The Evanston Police Department said in a statement that at around 9:49 a.m., the department received a call about two men having an argument and someone saying that a person was being taken into custody. Officers were dispatched to the 1700 block of Howard Street.

ABC 7 Chicago spoke with Miguel Olivares, who said he was on his break at El Pueblito Mexican Grill on Howard Street when he saw vehicles outside the restaurant and a confrontation taking place.

“It looked like police vehicles until I started hearing, ‘I’m a U.S. citizen. I’m a U.S. citizen,'” Olivares told the outlet.

Olivares said he recorded the incident on his phone, adding that the federal officers “were being rough with [the man]; they had him pinned against the floor, and it looked like one of the agents hit him in the face.”

He told NBC 5 Chicago that because it appeared the men really hurt the man, “we had to call 911.”

Officers arrived and found several people assisting the man on the ground, Evanston police said. He was found with injuries to the head, neck and teeth, prompting police to call for an ambulance. Witnesses told police that they believed ICE tried to detain the man.

Another Evanston police officer encountered two SUVs near Dodge Avenue and Brummel Street, the department said. An individual from one SUV wore plain clothes and a vest marked “‘POLICE’ with federal law enforcement markings” and identified himself as a federal officer “conducting a fugitive investigation,” according to police.

“The agent told the officer that agents had attempted to identify an individual who resembled a person they were seeking,” police stated. “He said the individual refused to provide identification, was detained for finerprinting and resisted detention. Agents later determined he was not the person they were seeking and learned that he was a U.S. citizen. He was released.”

The ICE officer said that five federal agents were operating in separate vehicles in the area, and he said the person they were looking for had addresses “associated with Chicago” and that there was a warrant for the man’s arrest, police said.

The police officer noticed blood on the hands of the ICE officer, who said he was injured while trying to handcuff the man. He declined medical treatment. ICE left the area where the incident took place after protesters appeared, as the federal officers “feared they would be attacked,” according to police. The injured man was hospitalized and met with Evanston Police Chief Schenita Stewart at the hospital to provide him with any support that he would need.

Police are investigating the incident and are collecting all body camera and dash camera footage, as well as photographs and video from witnesses. The department said that anyone with information about the incident is encouraged to contact police.

The DHS spokesperson told The Hill that its operations are “highly targeted.”

“We know who we are targeting ahead of time,” the spokesperson said. “If and when we do encounter individuals subject to arrest, our law enforcement is trained to ask a series of well-determined questions to determine status and removability.”

articles.body:
Melania Trump is teasing a forthcoming docuseries that she says will be “very different” from her eponymous documentary, and in which she’ll open up and answer “private” questions.

“It’s more conversation, one-on-one with me,” Trump said of the project during a Wednesday interview on Fox News’s “Fox and Friends.”

“When I was traveling and doing all of the filming, the director was asking me questions, and there are some private questions that I will answer that people never heard before,” she added.

“It will come out this year, and it will be very different [than] what is in the movie,” Trump said. The first lady added that while an exact date for the docuseries’s premiere hadn’t been set, it would likely be released in November.

The debut of the series comes nearly a year after the theatrical premiere of “Melania,” the Brett Ratner-directed film which followed Trump in the 20 days leading up to the 2025 presidential inauguration. Trump served as an executive producer of the $40 million documentary from Amazon MGM Studios, which also reportedly included a $35 million marketing campaign.

Trump told ITK at the “Melania” world premiere at the Kennedy Center in January that cameras followed her “day and night” for the feature film.

In August, Ratner wrote on Instagram that he couldn’t “wait to share with everyone around the world the next two chapters of Melania, the docuseries!”

Trump confirmed on Wednesday that a pair of installments would make up the series.

The 56-year-old “Melania” author — in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly as part of her Fostering the Future Together initiative and to launch her new effort , Imperia, aimed at advancing leadership and “economic power for women” — also gave her critique of President Trump’s remarks at the annual gathering. In his speech, Trump defended the U.S. war with Iran and said he was “not going to stifle growth” around artificial intelligence.

“I told him he had great delivery, he did very well, and a great speech,” Trump said.

“Sometimes he doesn’t want to hear it, what I tell him, but that’s OK. I always say the truth.”

articles.title: McConnell leads 4 GOP senators in calling for Trump to release Taiwan arms funding
articles.summary: Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) and three other Republican senators are calling on Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to release billions of dollars in stalled national security assistance for Taiwan, reminding the senior Cabinet officials of their past statements in support of defending Taiwan’s sovereignty. The senators in a letter…
articles.body:
Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) and three other Republican senators are calling on Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to release billions of dollars in stalled national security assistance for Taiwan, reminding the senior Cabinet officials of their past statements in support of defending Taiwan’s sovereignty.

The senators in a letter dated Wednesday cited the State Department’s intention not to obligate $300 million in foreign military financing, the failure of the Defense Department to obligate $1 billion in funding for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative and the administration’s decision to withhold $14 billion in foreign military sales to Taiwan.

The GOP senators expressed alarm over President Trump’s description of Taiwan as “a very good negotiating chip” in negotiations with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist Party.

“It is difficult to imagine how the United States might credibly project influence in the Indo-Pacific if the price of keeping up diplomatic appearances is denying our partners key deterrent capabilities,” the senators wrote, drawing a comparison to the fallout from former President Biden’s decision to withhold military assistance to Ukraine before a summit meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2021.

“Individually, instances of delayed or denied assistance test the strength of a security relationship you have described as essential,” the senators wrote.

“Together, despite your personal assurances earlier this year that Taiwan is not on the table in talks between President Trump and President Xi, they leave us with serious concerns about the strength of U.S. commitments to key partners and allies in Asia and across the globe,” they added.

Sens. John Cornyn (R-Texas), Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) and Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) also signed the letter.

McConnell, who led the effort, is the chair of the Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee. McConnell returned to the Senate this month after a long health-related absence.

The senators asked Rubio to explain why the State Department has not obligated $300 million in appropriated funding for Taiwan and asked Hegseth to explain why the Defense Department has not obligated $1 billion in funding for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative.

The GOP senators reminded Rubio that he previously played a “vocal role” in “marshalling congressional support for deeper and more unflinching security cooperations with Taiwan.”

And they noted to Hegseth that he once declared that the United States “will not let our allies and partners be subordinated and intimidated” and that “the threat China poses is real.”

The senators sent the letter to Rubio and Hegseth ahead of a two-day summit in Washington between Trump, Xi and senior U.S. and Chinese officials.

articles.title: Don’t assume moderate Democrats crave centrism
articles.summary: A voter can call themselves moderate and still want candidates who champion economic populism and challenge the political establishment.
articles.body:
Another election cycle, another round of well-resourced, centrist groups recycling the same arguments you could have overheard renting movies from Blockbuster in the ‘90s.

Because a plurality of voters identify themselves as “moderate,” they say , the path to winning elections is a version of “combative centrism” — pick fights with Trump, but also nominate candidates who break with the left, avoid promises of transformative change and don’t sound too threatening to corporate and wealthy interests.

It is an argument we have all heard before, and one that relies on oversimplifying what voters actually mean when they call themselves “moderate.”

The evidence that centrism itself is an electoral advantage is mixed and considerably weaker than its advocates suggest. As data journalist G. Elliott Morris has documented, claims about the electoral benefits of moderation are often overstated . Moderate Democrats may perform slightly better than a typical Democrat, but the estimated advantage is small and surrounded by considerable uncertainty.

More importantly, moderate is a description of how voters see themselves, not a prescriptive policy platform. It’s wrong to assume that voters think about ideology or see a choice between a centrist candidate and a progressive candidate in the same way political pundits and operatives do. A voter can call themselves moderate and still want candidates who champion economic populism and challenge the political establishment.

Recent public opinion research has made clear that voters, including moderates, are deeply skeptical of concentrated wealth and corporate power.

When the organization I lead, Data for Progress, asked which entities have the most negative impact on U.S. society and our economy, likely voters nationwide point to billionaires, corporate landlords and artificial intelligence companies. Among voters who identify as moderate, a majority say the existence of billionaires is a sign of a dysfunctional economy, and that billionaires earned their wealth through exploiting workers and consumers or through luck and family inheritance, rather than hard work and innovation.

The same pattern emerges in the most competitive congressional districts. The Working Families Party’s research finds that 80 percent of voters across 18 toss-up districts and Michigan believe elected officials care more about wealthy donors than people like them. More than half of moderates and independents in those districts prefer candidates who challenge the status quo and take on corporations and billionaires over candidates who defend the political establishment.

That is not a constituency clamoring for more conventional centrism. Our report on swing voters tells a similar story. We find that a majority of 2026 swing voters, 56 percent, call themselves moderate. But when we provide them with a list of policies and ask which three policies would make them definitely vote for a Democratic candidate in the midterm elections, they are persuaded more strongly by progressive economic policies than conservative cultural stances.

The top choice is to raise taxes on the wealthy at 28 percent, followed by creating a Medicare for All healthcare system at 24 percent. Also, 21 percent also choose to ban AI from setting prices or wages based on personal data, and 20 percent want to restrict private utility companies from passing unreasonable costs to customers.

Swing voters are not asking Democrats to split the difference on every issue. They want Democrats to advance tangible solutions to lower the cost of living and take on the powerful interests they believe are responsible for making their lives harder.

Centrism can backfire. In our polling, a hypothetical Democrat running on a populist economic message beat a Republican by 15 points , while a Democrat running on a more conventional Democratic message won by just 6 points. In other general election matchups, our polling has found Democratic candidates who reject corporate PAC money outperform candidates who who accept money from interests like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, AI, crypto and Big Pharma.

The lesson isn’t that every voter is secretly a socialist. It’s that the center of public opinion is not synonymous with the center of the political establishment.

That is also what makes the phrase combative centrism so revealing. Combativeness has to be directed at something. You cannot promise to fight the status quo while defending the incrementalism that sustains it. And you cannot credibly run as a populist champion for the working class while taking money from the same powerful interests you promise to fight.

Moving right for the sake of moving right will not bring moderates and swing voters into the Democratic coalition. The voters Democrats need are looking for candidates who will lower costs, put workers first and take on concentrated economic power.

Moderate voters aren’t asking Democrats to do less. They are asking them to make their lives better and take on the powerful interests standing in their way. They are asking them to do something that works.

Ryan O’Donnell is executive director of Data for Progress .

articles.title: Explosive new report puts Jack Smith back in hot seat as Jim Jordan alleges he tried to 'sway' 2024 election
articles.summary: Chairman Jim Jordan accuses Jack Smith and the DOJ of seizing 44 lawmakers' phone records while skirting Speech or Debate Clause protections.
articles.body: House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, is accusing former special counsel Jack Smith and the former Biden administration of trying to "sway" the 2024 election with the Department of Justice (DOJ) probe into President Donald Trump and his allies. "The Special Counsel’s prosecutors tried to silence President Trump with unlawful gag orders, threatened defense attorneys, mishandled key documents, and broke protocol to release a massive trove of alleged evidence just weeks before the presidential election to sway public opinion," the report said. "Although PIN cautioned that the subpoenas could be unconstitutional, PIN approved them nonetheless, asserting there was little 'litigation risk' because the gag orders that accompanied the subpoenas would prevent Members from ever discovering the seizures. As a result, Members of Congress were unaware of the Biden-Harris DOJ’s spying for more than two years." The report said investigators in the probe, colloquially known as "Arctic Frost," sought Jordan's own phone records from the period between August 2020 and January 2021 in relation to the federal probe into Rep. Scott Perry, R-Pa. An email excerpt showed PIN Deputy Chief Jennifer Clarke noted there was a "litigation risk" with the argument but "approved the subpoenas nonetheless," the report said. A separate email excerpt in the report showed another PIN official, John Keller, also said there was a "litigation risk" in obtaining members of Congress' toll records but noted it would be "minimal" due to the low likelihood of those lawmakers facing federal charges. JACK SMITH HIT WITH CRIMINAL REFERRAL AS GOP MOVES TESTIMONY FIGHT TOWARD PROSECUTION Keller's email also noted the government had a "potentially meritorious argument that the calls over the relevant period — especially unsolicited incoming calls — would not constitute protected legislative acts." The report also alleged that the DOJ ran afoul of its own rules by improperly using an independent watchdog office to serve Jordan's phone carrier when it significantly expanded what information it needed about him. "On May 1, the DOJ issued a subpoena for Chairman Jordan’s phone records from January 1, 2020, to April 25, 2022—every call incoming and outgoing for more than two years.43 A Special Agent from the DOJ Office of the Inspector General (OIG)—an entity that should be independent of the DOJ and maintain a reporting relationship with Congress as it investigates waste, fraud, and abuse—served the subpoena to Chairman Jordan’s phone carrier," the report said. OIG Special Agent Brian Burnett testified to the committee that the investigation as a whole was "unique" within his three decades of law enforcement experience in that he was following orders from an assistant U.S. attorney rather than investigating himself, the report alleged. "A normal investigation would be, I would do the investigation, become familiar with everything, you know, do grand jury subpoenas, do the normal investigative process, follow the normal investigative steps. But, in this case, those steps were given to us by the prosecution team," an excerpt from Burnett's testimony showed. MIKE DAVIS: WHY CRIMINAL REFERRAL OF JACK SMITH WAS 100% JUSTIFIED Jordan's report also noted that Smith's team backed down from grand jury subpoenas sent to AT&T for two other lawmakers' phone records after the phone carrier questioned their legal basis. TRUMP DOJ WITHDRAWS SUBPOENAS TARGETING NEW YORK TIMES JOURNALISTS AMID LEAK PROBE "In May 2023, Special Counsel Smith sent AT&T a grand jury subpoena that included a request for phone records associated with AT&T accounts for two other members of Congress. However, when AT&T raised questions with ... Special Counsel Smith’s office concerning the legal basis for seeking records of members of Congress, the Special Counsel did not pursue the subpoena further, and no records were produced," a letter highlighted in the report said. Smith testified to congressional investigators that he did not "have any recollection of that," the report said. The report goes as far as to say Smith "admitted privately" to then-Attorney General Merrick Garland that lawmakers "likely have a valid Speech or Debate privilege immunizing them from compelled testimony," but that Garland still gave his "blessing" to Smith for subpoenas "compelling the production of Members’ protected legislative records." Jordan reaffirmed past GOP-led probes' conclusions that prosecutors improperly bypassed a DOJ "filter team" process to obtain the 44 lawmakers' and Trump officials' records. Of those 44 lawmakers, two were Democrats. In the report's conclusion, Jordan urged the House of Representatives to take up legislation led by Rep. Mike Kelly, R-Pa., barring any government entity from obtaining records — whether by subpoena, court order, warrant, or otherwise — that is likely to implicate the Speech or Debate Clause. The bill, the Congressional Records Protection Act, advanced through the House Judiciary Committee but has so far not gotten a House floor vote. Jordan argued it would not just protect members of Congress but the people they serve, too. "The Speech or Debate Clause protects not only legislators, but American citizens too. It guarantees that the people’s representatives in Congress may advocate effectively on their constituents’ behalf without the threat of interference or intimidation by the Executive Branch," the report argued. Smith has so far stood by his team's findings and maintained his innocence amid a barrage of GOP attacks. In his testimony to Republicans, he laid blame on Trump for prosecutors collecting GOP lawmakers' records. "I think who should be accountable for this is Donald Trump. So responsibility for why these records, why we collected them...that lies with Donald Trump," Smith said in a report excerpt. articles.title: Federal unions owe workers more transparency. Congress can help.
articles.summary: The answer is not to weaken employee rights, but to strengthen them.
articles.body:
The American Federation of Government Employees is asking Congress to listen to federal employees, protect their workplace rights and restore collective bargaining rights stripped by executive order. The union is right to press that case. But lawmakers should ask at the same time: How many of the employees that AFGE claims to represent actually chose it to represent them?

AFGE is the largest federal-employee union. It is currently pressing lawmakers to override the order stripping bargaining rights from agencies covering roughly 70 percent of the workforce, and to restore bargaining rights for Defense civilians through the pending National Defense Authorization Act. AFGE says it represents more than 820,000 federal and D.C. employees.

AFGE’s own 2025 financial disclosures , filed with the Labor Department’s Office of Labor-Management Standards , tells a more complicated story: It has only about 225,000 dues-paying members, or 27.5 percent of those it is representing.

Other large unions’ filings look different. My analysis of labor management reports and the number of employees cited by unions showed that the Service Employees International Union converts close to 97 percent of represented workers into members. The Teamsters convert about 90 percent. The National Treasury Employees Union, another all-federal union, converts more than 70 percent.

Represented-worker counts are self-reported and unverified, so the gap could be narrower than it looks, but sector alone is unlikely to explain it.

The gap matters because only members elect the officers who negotiate labor contracts or communicate with Congress or the executive branch. Based on my experience, turnout in AFGE elections generally runs 30 to 35 percent of members, and sometimes lower. Multiply the figures, and in some cases fewer than one in 10 employees covered by a contract actually has a say in who speaks for them and how union dues are used. An equally thin slice of engaged members often selects the delegates who ultimately choose the union’s national officers.

Low turnout alone isn’t sinister; apathy is common to every membership organization. But apathy that persists for years under the same leadership stops looking like a mishap. An organization that cannot persuade a majority of the people it claims to represent to join isn’t demonstrating strength. It’s revealing that it hasn’t given most of them a reason to.

‘This is not an argument against unions or against AFGE’s case to Congress. Much of what AFGE is asking Congress to fix deserves support. It is an argument against unaccountable institutional power. The two problems are connected. A labor movement that can point to high, verified participation and transparent elections carries more weight when it argues that stripping bargaining rights is illegitimate. A movement with murky accountability numbers hands its opponents an easy rebuttal.

Had Congress modernized these guardrails years ago, AFGE and its peers might be standing on firmer ground today, instead of fighting the rollback while also fielding questions about who empowered them to fight it. The tools to fix this already exist. The Labor Department has cleared the way for remote electronic voting that meets certain standards, letting members vote directly on important union matters no matter how many or where they are. This requires no new technology — only for unions to use the tools already approved.

Congress should also ask why so few have and strengthen union accountability by requiring unions to disclose in their filings the total number of workers they claim to represent versus the number of actual members. They should also be required to report election turnout data at all levels: eligible voters, ballots sent and ballots returned — similar to shareholder-vote disclosures.

For example, some unions use “delegate” qualification procedures that can insulate national incumbents from direct member voting. As a matter of fair competition, challengers should have the same access to membership contact lists as incumbents, with sufficient time to mount a campaign, with direct member voting as the preferred standard.

Major national officer elections and financial decisions should go directly to the membership, not layers of delegates chosen by that same thin slice of members. Congress should also let the Federal Labor Relations Authority permit recertification/affiliation change votes at individual workplaces, when dues-paying membership remains a distinct minority of the workforce for a sustained period. This supports democracy.

This is a federal workplace, financed in part by taxpayer-paid official time, not a private-sector profit operation. Federal employees should have a direct voice in choosing their representatives and in how their dues, drawn from public service, are used. This would only impact unions with low membership rates.

The answer is not to weaken employee rights, but to strengthen them. A union officer is an elected representative — not the permanent custodian of an institution.

Federal employees deserve protection from arbitrary government action. A labor movement strong enough to demand it must also have the legitimacy to speak for its members. That legitimacy begins with leaders who are meaningfully and transparently chosen by the people they represent. Congress has a say in this for the federal workforce. It’s time to update labor law.

Javier Soto spent 10 years representing federal employees and unions, including five years as a Legal Rights Attorney at AFGE District 14.
